div.head: ECf retr 30.4a
div.ab: Uel, ut magis expresse secundum linguam Anglicam dicamus, wapentac: armorum tactus; wapen enim arma sonat, tac tactus est.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 653 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.
Liebermann prints 30, 4a and 30, 4b, which ECf lacks, in the larger type of the ECf column.

note.seg: confirma[tio] ward bezeugt durch vapnatak, Nordisch ‘Waffenanrühren der Versammlung’; tac heisst Nordisch ‘Griff, Fassen, Nehmen’. Schon Ann. Anglosax. seit 1075 braucht aber das Lehnwort tacan; Verf. meint also vielleicht irrig Angelsachsen nicht allein Nordischer Herkunft. — Den Retr. (vgl. 35, 1c: expressius dicimus) verführt Gleichklang mit dem Lateinischen zum Irrthum, es gebe ein *tac: Berührung

confirma[tio] was attested by vapnatak, Norse ‘touching of weapons by the assembly’; tac in Norse means ‘grip, grasping, taking’. But the Anglo-Saxon annals already use the loanword tacan from 1075; so the author perhaps wrongly means Anglo-Saxons not solely of Norse origin. — Similarity of sound with the Latin leads the Retractator (cf. 35, 1c: expressius dicimus) into the error that there is a *tac: touch

div.ab: Or, to say it more exactly according to the English tongue, wapentac: touching of arms; for wapen means arms, tac is touching.
